import Definitions.Def_AbcAdaptation_Reference_Iut_Tripod_CurveProviderHeight
import Definitions.Def_AbcAdaptation_Reference_Genl_Mathlib_Order_BoundedDiscrepancy

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod

open AbcAdaptation.Reference

variable (P : CurveProviders) (K : CompactlyBounded)

/-- **IUT IV, Corollary 2.2(i)** ([GenEll], Proposition 3.4): `(1/6)·log(q_∀) ≈ ht_{𝒪(1)}`
on a compactly bounded subset. -/
def LegendreHeightHyp : Prop := ((1 / 6 : ℝ) • P.h) ≈[K.set] htCan

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod
natural_language_statement: Fix an actual Legendre curve provider $P$ and a compactly bounded set $K$. Write $h_P(x)=P.h(x)$ for the provider's normalized Tate height and $H(x)=\mathrm{htCan}(x)$ for the absolute logarithmic Weil height. `LegendreHeightHyp P K` means that $h_P/6$ and $H$ have bounded discrepancy on $K$. The proposition asserts that there exist real constants $C_1,C_2$ such that, for every $x\in K$, $h_P(x)/6\leq H(x)+C_1$ and $H(x)\leq h_P(x)/6+C_2$. The constants are uniform over points of any degree.
